item.title: Chili
item.description: Five chilis that work in different ways: a whole-chile Texas bowl of red, a chili-cut beef and bean pot, a tomatillo pork braise, a spiced Cincinnati meat sauce, and a vegan black bean chili.

item.title: Black bean and sweet potato chili
item.description: Black beans simmered in a purée of toasted ancho and chipotle, built on cremini mushrooms cooked until they brown and stick, which gives the pot the savory depth that meat would. Sweet potato is roasted separately so it caramelizes and keeps its shape instead of dissolving.

item.title: Chile verde con puerco
item.description: Pork shoulder seared in lard and braised in a salsa of broiled tomatillos, poblano, Anaheim, and jalapeño chiles. The tomatillos supply both the acid and the body; charring them first trades their raw sourness for a sweeter, smoky depth.

item.title: Chunky beef and bean chili
item.description: Store-bought chili-cut beef, salted ahead and browned in bacon fat, braised with a purée of toasted ancho, guajillo, and chipotle in adobo, then finished with kidney beans and a masa-thickened gravy. A shorter braise than a whole-chuck chili because the pieces are small, and a lid on the pot because chili-cut packs often include leaner round.

item.title: Cincinnati chili
item.description: Ground beef broken into cold water rather than browned, so it cooks into a fine, saucy texture, then simmered for hours with ancho, cinnamon, allspice, cloves, cumin, and cocoa. Served over spaghetti under a heap of finely shredded cheddar, in the Greek-Macedonian tradition of Cincinnati chili parlors.

item.title: Basque burnt cheesecake
item.description: The La Viña tarta de queso from San Sebastián: cream cheese, sugar, eggs, heavy cream and a spoonful of flour, baked crustless in a parchment-lined springform at high heat until the top scorches nearly black and the center stays a loose, creamy custard. Five ingredients, one bowl, and the oven does the work.

item.title: Zhajiangmian (Beijing fried-sauce noodles)
item.description: Diced pork belly rendered in a wok, then fried slowly in a 2:1 blend of yellow soybean paste and sweet bean sauce until the paste darkens and the oil separates out around it. The salty, glossy sauce goes over hot fresh wheat noodles with piles of raw cucumber and radish, blanched sprouts and edamame, and raw garlic and black vinegar at the table.

item.title: Birria de res with consomé
item.description: Beef chuck and oxtail marinated overnight in a guajillo, ancho, and chile de árbol adobo with vinegar, toasted spices, and charred tomato, then braised for four hours until the meat falls apart and the bones have turned the liquid into a glossy, gelatin-rich consomé. Served as tacos on fat-dipped, griddled corn tortillas with a cup of consomé for dipping.

item.title: Butter chicken (murgh makhani)
item.description: Boneless chicken thighs marinated in spiced yogurt, charred hard under the broiler in place of a tandoor, then simmered briefly in a silky tomato, cashew, and butter gravy finished with crushed kasuri methi and cream. The gravy is blended and reduced until it clings, so it reads rich and tangy rather than sweet.

item.title: Caldo verde
item.description: The Portuguese kale and potato soup: potatoes simmered with onion, garlic, and a whole chouriço, puréed smooth with olive oil, then finished with collards sliced so thin they cook in four minutes. Served with slices of the poached chouriço and a thread of raw olive oil on top.

item.title: Champurrado
item.description: The Mexican chocolate atole: masa harina whisked into milk and water steeped with canela, sweetened with piloncillo and Mexican chocolate, and cooked until the corn starch thickens it to a pourable, velvety body. Thick enough to coat a spoon, thin enough to drink from a mug.

item.title: Chicken pot pie
item.description: Bone-in thighs poached gently in chicken stock, and that enriched poaching liquid becomes the velouté that binds browned mushrooms, carrot, parsnip, celery, and peas. Dry sherry and a squeeze of lemon keep the cream sauce bright, and an all-butter puff pastry lid bakes up crisp over the hot filling.

item.title: Chilaquiles rojos with fried eggs
item.description: Corn tortilla wedges fried into totopos, then tossed for thirty seconds in a guajillo-ancho-tomato salsa that has been fried in hot oil until it darkens and thickens. Topped with crisp-edged fried eggs, crema, queso fresco, raw white onion, and cilantro, so each bite moves between crunch, soft chip, and runny yolk.

item.title: Çılbır
item.description: Turkish poached eggs set on a bed of thick, garlicky strained yogurt at room temperature, then drowned in butter that has been lightly browned and stained brick red with pul biber. Finished with dill and eaten with bread to drag through the yogurt, yolk, and butter.

item.title: Dal tadka
item.description: Toor dal pressure-cooked soft, whisked smooth, simmered into an onion-tomato masala, then finished at the table with a second tadka of ghee, cumin, sliced garlic, dried red chili, asafoetida, and Kashmiri chili poured over the top. This is the North Indian dhaba version: two rounds of tempering, one cooked into the dal and one sizzling on top, with lime to sharpen it.

item.title: Dolsot bibimbap
item.description: Short-grain rice pressed into a sesame-oiled stone bowl, crowned with five individually seasoned namul (spinach, soybean sprouts, carrot, zucchini, shiitake), soy-glazed ground beef, and a fried egg, then heated until the bottom layer fries into a crackling golden crust. A gochujang, sesame, and rice vinegar sauce is stirred in at the table. Instructions for a cast-iron skillet are included for cooks without a stone bowl.

item.title: Dutch baby with lemon and powdered sugar
item.description: A thin egg-rich batter blended at room temperature and poured into a smoking-hot buttered cast-iron skillet, where steam puffs it into a tall, crisp-edged pancake with a custardy center. Finished at the table with fresh lemon juice and powdered sugar.

item.title: Empanadas mendocinas
item.description: Baked beef empanadas in the style of Mendoza: a lard dough wrapped around hand-cut beef cooked with an equal weight of onion, sweet paprika, cumin, and ají molido, with hard-boiled egg and green olive in every one. The filling is made the day before and chilled so the fat sets, which keeps it juicy inside the pastry, and each empanada is sealed with a braided repulgue edge.

item.title: Falafel
item.description: Levantine chickpea falafel made the way the street stalls make it: dried chickpeas soaked overnight and ground raw with a large volume of parsley, cilantro, onion, and garlic, so the interior fries up loose, fluffy, and bright green inside a dark, crackling shell. Served in warm pita with tahini sauce, tomato, cucumber, pickled turnip, and herbs.

item.title: Feijoada
item.description: Brazilian black beans simmered for about two and a half hours with desalted carne seca, smoked pork ribs, linguiça, and slab bacon until the beans collapse into a dark, glossy, pork-rich broth. Served the Rio way, with white rice, garlicky shredded collards, buttered farofa, a sharp lime and chili bean sauce, and orange slices to cut the fat.

item.title: Gong bao chicken (Sichuan kung pao chicken)
item.description: Diced chicken thigh in a light starch marinade, stir-fried hard in oil that has bloomed dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns, then tossed with scallion, garlic, and ginger in a thin sweet-sour glaze of Chinkiang vinegar and soy. Roasted peanuts go in last so they stay crisp; the sauce clings, it does not pool.

item.title: Gratin dauphinois
item.description: Thin, unrinsed Yukon Gold slices simmered in garlic-infused milk and cream until the released starch thickens the liquid, then baked low and slow in a garlic-rubbed dish until tender and bronzed. No cheese, as in the Dauphiné: the potato starch and reduced cream make the sauce on their own.

item.title: Hong Kong French toast (sai dor si)
item.description: Two thick crustless slices of white bread sandwiched with peanut butter, dipped in beaten egg, and fried in a shallow pool of hot oil until puffed and deep golden. Served the cha chaan teng way, with a cold slab of butter melting on top and golden syrup poured over.

item.title: Hong shao rou (Shanghai red-braised pork belly)
item.description: Skin-on pork belly blanched clean, glazed in a rock-sugar caramel, then braised low for 90 minutes in Shaoxing wine with light and dark soy. The liquid is boiled down at the end until it coats every cube in a sticky mahogany lacquer and the fat trembles under a chopstick.

item.title: Hyderabadi chicken dum biryani
item.description: Bone-in chicken marinated in yogurt, green chili, mint, and fried onions, cooked through into a thick masala, then buried under basmati boiled to 70 percent and sealed with dough to finish in its own steam. This is the pakki (cooked-meat) method: the chicken is fully cooked before the dum, so the sealed steam only has to finish the rice and marry the layers.

item.title: Japanese chicken curry rice (kare raisu)
item.description: Salted chicken thighs seared in a Dutch oven, onions caramelized in the fond to deep amber, then carrot, potato, grated apple, and chicken stock simmered until tender and thickened with a from-scratch butter-flour roux cooked to golden brown with curry powder and garam masala bloomed in it. Thick, glossy, gently sweet, and savory, served beside short-grain rice with fukujinzuke.

item.title: Kardemummabullar (Swedish cardamom buns)
item.description: Soft, lightly sweet Swedish buns with freshly ground cardamom in both the dough and the butter-sugar filling, folded, cut into strips, twisted into knots and finished with pearl sugar. Grinding the seeds yourself is what makes them smell the way they do in a Stockholm bakery.

item.title: Khachapuri adjaruli
item.description: The Adjarian boat from Georgia's Black Sea coast: a soft milk-yeast dough rolled into a canoe, filled with a salty, molten blend of stretchy and crumbly cheeses, and baked very hot until the rims blister. A raw yolk and a pat of butter go in at the end, and the whole thing is stirred at the table and eaten by tearing off the crust to dip.

item.title: Kimchi jjigae
item.description: Sour, well-fermented napa kimchi stir-fried in rendered pork belly fat with gochugaru and garlic, then simmered in anchovy-kelp stock with its own brine until the pork is tender and the broth turns deep red and tangy. Tofu goes in last and drinks the broth. A 40-minute weeknight stew whose acidity, funk, and heat all come from the kimchi itself.

item.title: Nasi lemak
item.description: Malaysian coconut rice steamed with pandan, ginger, and lemongrass, served with sambal ikan bilis (a dried-chili and shallot paste fried slowly until the oil splits, then sharpened with tamarind and sweetened with palm sugar), crisp fried anchovies and peanuts, cucumber, and a boiled egg. The sambal is the work and the reason the plate tastes like itself.
